step_by_step_reasoning:
The architecture depicts GumGum's Verity contextual intelligence platform operating across an AWS Main Region and AWS Outposts for low-latency ad contextual classification.

1. Main Region Standard Flow:
- Web/API clients send web page classification requests (e.g., gumgum.com) to API Gateway.
- API Gateway passes requests to the RESTful API running on Main Region EKS.
- Main Region EKS checks DynamoDB (holding 15TB of classification data) for existing entries.

2. AI Contextual Classification Loop:
- On cache miss in DynamoDB, an orchestrator component on EKS triggers the GumGum AI stack on ECS (composed of NLP and Computer Vision microservices).
- ECS microservices process content and update classification results into DynamoDB until complete.

3. Data Replication:
- Data is continuously synchronized in real-time from DynamoDB in the Main Region to ElastiCache Redis (1TB) located on AWS Outposts.

4. Low-Latency Edge API Flow (AWS Outposts):
- Low-latency clients requiring sub-10ms SLA at 100k req/sec connect to the ALB on AWS Outposts.
- ALB routes requests to the Edge API (built in Go) on Outpost EKS.
- Edge API performs sub-10ms cache lookups against ElastiCache Redis.
- On cache miss at the edge, Edge API sends an orchestration request back to Main Region EKS to kick off the full AI classification loop.
